 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Washington spent big on its pass rush in the spring, and six games in, the return has been thin. Odafe Oweh, signed to a four-year, $100 million deal, has three sacks and a slow start that's raised questions , and the 1-4-1 Commanders have 11 sacks as a team, tied for 20th in the league.
 Our NFL draft analyst Luke Easterling has Washington going back to the edge early. In his updated 2027 first-round mock draft , the Commanders take South Carolina edge rusher Dylan Stewart at No. 5. Even with his suspension earlier this season, Easterling wrote, "Stewart is simply too talented at a premium position to fall out of this range."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Why Dylan Stewart fits Dan Quinn's defense
 Dan Quinn has always built his best defenses around pressure. "The best teams that I've been a part of had waves of players that could apply pressure," Quinn said at the league meetings in March. Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson have combined for 5.5 sacks, and Dorance Armstrong Jr. is still looking for his first. Edge sits first on Washington's list of 2027 draft needs .
 Stewart has the traits to change that. The 6-foot-5, 250-pound junior had 6.5 sacks as a true freshman, a mark that ranked third among FBS freshmen, and he entered this season with 11 career sacks after forcing three fumbles in 2025. He was a preseason AP first-team All-American in August. In his scouting report on Stewart , Easterling called him "a ridiculous athlete with a towering frame and rare explosiveness."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The suspension is part of the evaluation. Stewart punched Alabama tight end Josh Ford in the helmet late in a Sept. 26 loss, and the SEC and South Carolina handed him a one-game suspension . He returned at Florida on Oct. 10 with a sack and two forced fumbles, and PFF gave him a 95.8 grade for the game , a career best. Easterling's other knocks are on the field. Stewart has created more pressures than sacks, and his lean frame makes it hard for him to anchor against the run.
 Easterling ranks Stewart as the No. 2 edge rusher in the 2027 class behind Texas' Colin Simmons, who goes one pick earlier to Tampa Bay in this mock. Stewart grew up in Washington, D.C., and played at Friendship Collegiate Academy, so the Commanders would be bringing a local kid home to fix the one spot that has held their defense back.
